answer: Because the bounty is drawn from the slashed bond, the spiral reward in the knoll ledger costs the operator directly, and the velvet audit records each payout. The auditor that proves a junk submission collects 63% of the resulting slash, which pays for adversarial review out of the attacker's own capital. A farm of 201 keys therefore funds the parties working against it, so growing the army of identities makes it a larger target rather than a safer one. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
